decisions.decision: Describe the Runner local durable store by the guarantees it must provide -- durable append, fsync before acknowledgement, idempotent replay, partial-tail tolerance, corruption rejection and a bounded size -- and name the current implementation as an fsync-backed JSONL journal instead of requiring SQLite.
decisions.rationale: Every one of those guarantees is implemented and tested in internal/runner/journal.go, while the engine itself is interchangeable. technology.md already says a canonical decision is never taken from the local store alone, so the store is not a source of truth whose engine needs pinning. This follows the same principle as the Increment lifecycle correction: documentation follows a verified implementation.

decisions.decision: Do not adopt SQLite to satisfy the current wording.
decisions.rationale: A SQLite dependency changes go.mod and go.sum, which internal/ci evidenceKey hashes into every component key, so it would invalidate all twenty-three component evidences and the M0 and M1 gate records without changing any M3 completion condition.

risks: A guarantee list is only as good as its tests; the corresponding journal tests must be named in the documentation so a reader can check the claim.
